title: Design facility controls as coordinated layers: concept decisions 1
teachingQuestion: Which coordinated facility control set protects this asset, and what response makes it effective?
focalInsight: Facility safeguards need maintenance, monitoring, accountable response, and test evidence.
caption: Read across a row to connect meaning, decision and consequence. Use the retrieval answer to check your explanation after reading the linked scenario.

nodes.label: Wiring Closet Security
nodes.definition: Protection of cabling, network equipment, and intermediate distribution facilities.
nodes.detail: Protection of cabling, network equipment, and intermediate distribution facilities.
nodes.decision: Control entry, changes, cabling, environment, maintenance, and alert response.
nodes.failureExample: An unlocked closet lets an intruder connect a rogue network device.
nodes.retrievalAnswer: Network infrastructure needs physical and change control.

nodes.label: Data Center Security
nodes.definition: Layered protection of data-center facilities, equipment, operations, utilities, and maintenance.
nodes.detail: Layered protection of data-center facilities, equipment, operations, utilities, and maintenance.
nodes.decision: Combine entry controls, environment, power, zoning, operations separation, and response.
nodes.failureExample: A data center has strong doors but uncontrolled vendor maintenance access.
nodes.retrievalAnswer: Data center security includes the support and operations path.

nodes.label: Media Storage
nodes.definition: Controlled storage of removable media or data-bearing assets through inventory, access, retention, and disposal.
nodes.detail: Controlled storage of removable media or data-bearing assets through inventory, access, retention, and disposal.
nodes.decision: Use custody and protection based on classification, recovery risk, and lifecycle.
nodes.failureExample: Backup tapes sit in an unlocked office before offsite transfer.
nodes.retrievalAnswer: Media protection covers storage, movement, and end of life.

nodes.label: Evidence Storage
nodes.definition: Preservation of evidence with integrity, access control, retention, and chain of custody.
nodes.detail: Preservation of evidence with integrity, access control, retention, and chain of custody.
nodes.decision: Use when records may support investigation, legal, or disciplinary reliance.
nodes.failureExample: An incident log is copied among analysts with no custody record.
nodes.retrievalAnswer: Evidence must remain attributable and resistant to alteration.

nodes.label: Work Area Security
nodes.definition: Controls for normal work spaces, screens, documents, visitors, and local devices.
nodes.detail: Controls for normal work spaces, screens, documents, visitors, and local devices.
nodes.decision: Apply zoning, visitor rules, clean desk/display practices, and logical protection by sensitivity.
nodes.failureExample: A visitor photographs visible records from an unattended workstation.
nodes.retrievalAnswer: Work-area controls protect routine exposure paths.

nodes.label: Hvac
nodes.definition: Heating, ventilation, and air-conditioning capability affecting equipment environment and people.
nodes.detail: Heating, ventilation, and air-conditioning capability affecting equipment environment and people.
nodes.decision: Provide maintenance, monitoring, alarms, redundancy or response suited to thermal consequence.
nodes.failureExample: Cooling loss overheats equipment while no monitored alert reaches operators.
nodes.retrievalAnswer: HVAC is an availability and safety dependency.

nodes.label: Fire Suppression
nodes.definition: Detection and suppression or containment measures for fire risk.
nodes.detail: Detection and suppression or containment measures for fire risk.
nodes.decision: Select compatible detection, response, suppression, personnel safety, and asset effects.
nodes.failureExample: Suppression is installed but no tested alert/response process exists.
nodes.retrievalAnswer: Suppression works with detection and response, not alone.

nodes.label: Power Resilience
nodes.definition: Ability to sustain or safely recover power-dependent services through redundancy, backup, and maintenance.
nodes.detail: Ability to sustain or safely recover power-dependent services through redundancy, backup, and maintenance.
nodes.decision: Plan utility, UPS, generator, fuel, transfer, load priority, testing, and recovery.
nodes.failureExample: A generator has no fuel assurance or tested transfer under load.
nodes.retrievalAnswer: Power resilience is a maintained system, not a generator purchase.

nodes.label: Environmental Monitoring
nodes.definition: Sensing and alerting for temperature, humidity, water, smoke, power, or other conditions.
nodes.detail: Sensing and alerting for temperature, humidity, water, smoke, power, or other conditions.
nodes.decision: Connect monitored thresholds to accountable response and test the full signal path.
nodes.failureExample: A water sensor alarms locally but nobody receives or acts on it.
nodes.retrievalAnswer: Monitoring only reduces risk when it drives response.

learningContract.teachingQuestion: Which coordinated facility control set protects this asset, and what response makes it effective?
learningContract.misconception: Buying a generator, lock, alarm, or suppression system proves resilience.
learningContract.formRationale: Aligned comparisons force a distinction among scope, selection trigger, concrete failure, and retrieval response.
learningContract.focalInsight: Facility safeguards need maintenance, monitoring, accountable response, and test evidence.
learningContract.intentionalOmissions: Implementation settings and jurisdiction-specific conclusions are not inferred from these concise concept comparisons.
learningContract.retrievalPrompt: For the asset, name the control, the triggering condition, and the response or recovery evidence.
